channel.title: nexusEVnews
channel.description: Independent EV and renewable energy news, curated daily. Electric vehicles, solar, battery tech, and charging infrastructure.

item.title: The Battery Gets the Free Lunch
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Australia's free midday power mostly rewards homes that can store it, which is also the quiet argument behind Porsche's floor-mounted charging pad.

item.title: The Catch Was Somewhere Else
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A Polestar 2 sold as damaged, an electric Range Rover that tows less and an iX3 that drops lane centering: the real catch is rarely the advertised one.

item.title: Which One Did They Test?
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A Donut Lab cell, a Zeekr battery and an R2 on all-terrain tires: each headline number belongs to one version, and it may not be the one you buy.

item.title: The Old One Is Still in the Room
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Every new car in today's edition has to beat something older, and in a couple of cases, a used i7 or an early R2, the older version comes out ahead.

item.title: Weight Is Back on the Spec Sheet
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: An aircraft cell at 350 Wh/kg, a Roadster cell in an aluminum can and an A2 heavier than its 900 kg ancestor all make lightness a feature again.

item.title: The Default Decides
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A Tesla's map points to Superchargers, the MG5 leaves out V2L and the R2 skips CarPlay. Whoever chooses the default shapes what owners do next.

item.title: Listening Has a Lead Time
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Pebble can turn an owner's complaint into a production change in a week. Tesla's Roadster is still answering for 2017. How fast a company listens is now part of the car.

item.title: What You See Is Not What Changed
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: An Atto 3 that looks the same and is not, an iX4 whose new roofline costs boot space, and a charging network that grew without getting more reliable.

item.title: Compared to What?
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A solar panel that wins against a weak baseline, home batteries that win on storage and lose on power, and a used Ioniq 6 measured against $25,000.

item.title: Installed Is Not Delivered
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: China switches off wind and solar it already built, a Love's charging site holds 1,200 kW but gives one car 200, and Scout buyers want a generator anyway.

item.title: Proof Arrives in Stages
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A concept with no battery figure, two prototypes measured on good days, an RV on delivery day and an R2 after 1,178 miles: the evidence grows at each step.

item.title: Pick Your Weakness
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A buyer who chose slow charging over buggy software, a Tesla motor built around weaker magnets, and a truck battery that charges during the driver's mandatory break.

item.title: Repetition Is the Product
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A battery plant counts defects per billion, small reactors still wait for a second identical build, and BMW's new platform repeats its flaws along with its savings.

item.title: The Fine Print Picks the Car
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: An insurance quote picked an Ioniq 5, British wiring rules split Hoymiles' solar from its battery, and US policy shrank GM's Bolt run to a fraction.

item.title: Keep the Buttons, Lose the Full Tank
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: Volkswagen puts real dials back in its electric Tiguan, Polestar gives the 4 a rear window, and a veteran EV driver asks people to stop filling to the top.

item.title: The Distance Is in the Price
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A Semi plant that stamps its own panels, lithium pumped from beneath German farmland, and a Geely priced in yuan at home and in pounds here.

item.title: Most of the Price Is Optional
item.dc:creator: nexusEVnews
item.description: A €200,000 i7 that its reviewer says is not worth double the base car, a Lucid built on smaller wheels, and a Bentley calling 875 hp sufficient.

item.title: The Self-Driving Story Nobody Is Telling
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: The autonomy debate is all horse race. But for millions of people who cannot drive, a car that drives itself is the keys, handed back. Why Rivian's road to Level 4 matters more than the spec sheet, and the one thing it still has to get right.

item.title: Two Batteries, One Hitch, and the Case for All-Electric Glamping
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: The Lightship AE1 carries its own 69 kWh battery and 80 kW motor to neutralize trailer drag on the tow vehicle. Paired with a Rivian, the real-world efficiency numbers are hard to argue with. This is what all-electric glamping looks like when the hardware actually works.

item.title: Atlanta, Rivian, and the Quiet Coincidence
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hunka
item.description: Atlanta has a failing air quality grade and a Rivian plant on its doorstep. A hypothetical about what one city could do with the electric mobility infrastructure that already exists — R2 autonomous taxis, ALSO cargo quads, e-bikes, and ZTL-style restricted zones — and what the health data says the stakes actually are. Includes data from the HEI lockdown air quality study (Chen et al., 2025) and the American Lung Association's 2025 Atlanta air quality report.
